title: Fictional federal claim against Officer Alpha, individual capacity

parent.objective: Maintain a source-pinned claim matrix for one fictional federal claim against one defendant in one capacity.
parent.milestone: Claim matrix declared, citations linked, and governing and adverse authority read

goal: State the fictional claim's elements, evidence, threshold defense, adverse authority, remedy, limitations and justiciability, each resting on declared assertions.
non_goals: Predict the outcome of any claim or defense.
File, serve, or send anything to any person or court.

allowed: Declare the claim matrix and check every cited source resolves.
Record primary-source reviews of the governing and adverse authority.
prohibited: Cite a real statute, case, party, or authority.
Treat an allegation as fact before a bound primary-source review.
Omit adverse authority or a threshold defense.

acceptance_criteria.description: The claim names one defendant and one capacity, and every element is tied to evidence.
Every cited source resolves to a declared source and adverse authority is present.
The governing authority is checked against the fictional code's text.
The adverse authority is checked against the fictional case's text.

validation.description: Check the claim has one defendant and capacity and each element cites a non-legal assertion.

argv: claim = {'defendant': 'DEF-ALPHA', 'capacity': 'individual', 'elements': {'EL-COLOR': ['AS-COLOR-OF-LAW'], 'EL-DEPRIVATION': ['AS-DETENTION']}}; assert claim['capacity'] in ('individual', 'official') and all(claim['elements'].values()); print('claim matrix structured')

validation.description: Check every cited source id against the declared sources and confirm adverse authority is present.

argv: declared = {'SRC-CRN-COMPLAINT', 'SRC-CRN-ROSTER', 'SRC-CRN-DISPATCH-LOG', 'SRC-CRN-VIDEO', 'SRC-CRN-PAYROLL', 'SRC-CRN-CODE', 'SRC-CRN-LIMITATIONS-CODE', 'SRC-CRN-ADVERSE-ROE'}; cited = {'SRC-CRN-CODE', 'SRC-CRN-ADVERSE-ROE', 'SRC-CRN-LIMITATIONS-CODE'}; adverse = ['SRC-CRN-ADVERSE-ROE']; assert cited <= declared and adverse; print('citations linked, adverse authority present')

The derived claim or defendant matrix.

domain.forum: Fictional Synthetic District Court; forum label only, no jurisdiction determination.
domain.procedural_posture: Fictional pre-filing research; no proceeding has been commenced.

defendants.role: Patrol officer alleged to have conducted the fictional 2026-01-10 stop.

assertions.assertion: Officer Alpha was an on-duty Town of Gamma patrol officer during the fictional 2026-01-10 stop.
Under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 1, a claim requires conduct under color of state law that deprives a person of a protected right.
Officer Alpha stopped the plaintiff while dispatched on an official call.
Officer Alpha detained the plaintiff for forty minutes without a warrant.
Fictional Roe v. Placeholder holds that an officer is immune from damages unless fictional precedent clearly established the right at the time.
Whether fictional precedent clearly established the right on 2026-01-10 has not been researched.
Fictional Synthetic Limitations Code section 2 sets a three-year period for this claim.
The claim accrued on the fictional stop date, 2026-01-10.
Whether any tolling applies to the fictional limitations period has not been researched.
Under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 3, a person injured by a completed detention may seek damages.
The plaintiff lost a day's wages because of the detention.

claims.statement: Officer Alpha, in an individual capacity, detained the plaintiff without a warrant, depriving the plaintiff of a fictional protected right.
claims.legal_question: Does Officer Alpha's fictional forty-minute warrantless detention state a claim against Officer Alpha individually under fictional Synthetic Civil Rights Code section 1?
claims.right: Fictional right against unreasonable seizure (a stand-in that states no real constitutional holding).

elements.requirement: Conduct under color of state law.

missing_evidence.description: The fictional dash-camera recording has not been obtained.

threshold_defenses.defense: Individual-capacity immunity under fictional Roe v. Placeholder.
threshold_defenses.rebuttal: Research whether fictional precedent clearly established the right before the stop.

remedies.description: Lost wages for the day of the fictional detention.

limitations.prerequisites: No fictional notice or exhaustion prerequisite is declared for this claim in this worked example.

justiciability.standing: A completed fictional detention with a claimed wage loss, traceable to Officer Alpha and redressable by damages.
justiciability.mootness_and_prospective_relief: Damages only; no prospective relief is sought, so mootness does not arise.

claims.next_action: Obtain the fictional dash-camera recording and research fictional precedent on clearly established rights.
